questions: Let's talk about what you do. Do you work or are you a student?
What do you enjoy most about your work or studies?
Is there anything you would like to change about it?
Do you prefer to work or study in the morning or in the afternoon?
sampleAnswers: I'm a student. I'm currently doing a master's degree in international business, which I started last September after working for a couple of years in a marketing agency.

I really enjoy the case studies. We analyse real companies and debate what they should have done differently, and because my classmates come from so many countries, I get to hear perspectives I'd never have thought of.
I'd like a bit more practical experience. A lot of the course is quite theoretical, and I think an internship or a project with a real company would help us apply what we're learning.
Definitely the morning. My mind is much sharper before lunch, so I try to do the most demanding reading early on and leave things like emails and admin for the afternoon, when my energy dips.

questions: Now let's talk about walking. Do you walk a lot?
Where do you like to go for a walk?
Did you walk more when you were younger?
Do you think people should walk more in their daily lives?
sampleAnswers: Quite a lot, yes. I walk to the station every morning, which takes about fifteen minutes, and I often go for a walk in the evening to clear my head after studying.

There's a path along the river near my flat that I love. It's lined with trees and it's surprisingly peaceful considering it's right in the middle of the city. At the weekend I sometimes walk in the hills outside town.
I think I walked more, because I walked to school every day and spent hours playing outside. Then for a few years I relied on the bus, and it's only recently that I've rediscovered walking.

Absolutely. It's free, it's good for both your physical and mental health, and it doesn't pollute. Of course, it's easier in cities that are designed for pedestrians, so I think planners have a role to play too.

questions: Let's talk about where you live. Can you describe the place where you live?
What do you like about the area?
How long have you lived there?
What would your ideal home be like?
sampleAnswers: I live in a two-bedroom apartment on the third floor of a modern building, not far from the city centre. It's quite compact, but it's bright and it has a small balcony where I keep a few plants.

It's very convenient. There's a supermarket, a gym and a metro station all within five minutes' walk. There's also a lovely park nearby, which is great for a run or just to sit and read on a sunny day.
For about two years now. Before that I was living in a shared house on the other side of the city, which was cheaper but much further from everything I need.

Ideally, a house with a garden somewhere quiet but still well connected to the city. I'd love a room with big windows that I could use as a study, and a kitchen big enough to have friends round for dinner.

questions: Now let's talk about birthdays. Do you usually celebrate your birthday?
How did you celebrate your last birthday?
Were birthdays more important to you when you were a child?
Do you prefer to give or receive birthday presents?
sampleAnswers: Yes, but in a fairly low-key way. I'm not one for huge parties, so I usually have dinner with my closest friends or my family, which I find much more enjoyable.

My last birthday fell on a Saturday, so a group of friends and I went hiking in the morning and then had a long lunch at a restaurant in a village in the mountains. It was simple, but it was a lovely day.
Definitely. As a child I'd count down the days for weeks, mainly because of the presents and the cake. Now it's more of an excuse to get together with people I don't see often enough.

Giving, I think. I really enjoy finding something that suits a person perfectly, and seeing their reaction. Receiving presents is nice, of course, but I always feel slightly awkward opening them in front of people.
